name: Castelo dos Mouros
seoTitle: Moorish Castle Sintra: Worth It Instead of Pena?
tagline: Granite walls on the ridge beside Pena: the cheaper, untimed way to Sintra's big views, best on a clear day.

description.short: A 10th-century Islamic fortification on a ridge of the Sintra hills, restored by Ferdinand II in the 19th century. Bus 434 stops here just before Pena; the visit takes 60 to 90 minutes and is all outdoors.
description.full:
The Moorish Castle sits on the ridge just below Pena, and most cruise passengers who reach it treat it as an add-on: bus 434 stops at the castle and then at Pena, and the two entrances are a short walk apart on the same road. The more useful question is whether to visit it instead of Pena.

It is worth choosing over Pena if you mainly want the views. From the walls you look across to Pena itself, down to the town and the National Palace, and on clear days out to the Atlantic. There is no timed entry, the ticket is 12 euros against 20 for Pena's Essential Visit, and the visit is shorter, 60 to 90 minutes. Choose Pena if you want an interior: the castle is a walled ruin with no furnished rooms.

The visit is physical. The walls follow the rock, with uneven steps, steep stretches and drops beside the walkways, and the ridge is exposed to wind. In low cloud the views, which are the point of coming, disappear, so check the forecast before committing a long call to it.

Inside the walls are the Arms Square, where the garrison gathered; the Castle Keep at one of the highest points; grain silos cut into the rock; and the church of São Pedro de Canaferrim, now an interpretation centre with finds from the Neolithic to the Middle Ages. Nearby is the tomb Ferdinand II built for bones found during his restoration, inscribed 'What man brought together, only God may separate', because no one could tell whether they were Christian or Moorish.

From the Jardim do Tabaco terminal allow 75 to 90 minutes each way: metro to Restauradores, train from Rossio, then bus 434. The castle alone fits a call of seven to eight hours; with Pena as well, plan on about ten. Last entry is 17:30, earlier than at Pena.
description.history: The castle was founded in the 10th century, under Islamic rule, to watch over the land and sea approaches to Lisbon. A population lived inside and around the walls, storing grain in silos cut into the rock. In 1147, after Afonso Henriques took Lisbon and Santarém, Sintra surrendered to him, and in 1154 the Templar master Gualdim Pais received a charter for the town. A Christian village with the church of São Pedro de Canaferrim grew up between the two rings of walls, but it was gradually abandoned from the 15th century. In the 19th century Ferdinand II restored the walls in a Romantic spirit. Excavations have continued since 1976, and Parques de Sintra has managed the site since 2000.
description.significance: The castle shows two layers of Sintra's history at once: a 10th-century Islamic fortification built to control the approaches to Lisbon, and its 19th-century Romantic restoration by Ferdinand II, who made it part of the view from Pena. It is a key part of the Cultural Landscape of Sintra listed by UNESCO in 1995, and excavations here have documented occupation of the hills from the Neolithic to the Middle Ages.

directions.general: On a ridge of the Sintra hills between the historic centre and Pena. Private vehicles cannot drive to the castle.
directions.fromCruisePort: Walk about 10 minutes to Santa Apolónia and take the metro Blue Line to Restauradores; Rossio station is a two-minute walk. Trains from Rossio reach Sintra in about 40 minutes. From Sintra station take Scotturb bus 434, which stops at the castle before continuing to Pena. Allow 75 to 90 minutes door to door each way.
directions.publicTransport: Train from Lisbon Rossio to Sintra (about 40 minutes), then Scotturb bus 434 to the Castelo dos Mouros stop. On foot, the marked Santa Maria trail climbs from the historic centre to the castle (about 1.8 km, around an hour uphill).
directions.parking: Private vehicles are not allowed up to the castle. Park in the historic centre or the outer car parks and take bus 434 or walk.

distanceFromCruisePort.walkingTime: Not walkable from port - too far
distanceFromCruisePort.drivingTime: 45 minutes by car, 75-100 minutes by public transport

openingTimes.currentStatus: Open daily except 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January

seasonal.notes: Ticket office closed 12:00-13:00; ticket machines available

admissionPrices.notes: 2026 prices: adults 18-64 12 euros, youths 6-17 and seniors 65+ 10 euros, family (2 adults + 2 youths) 33 euros. The official price table does not list a fare for under-6s; confirm when booking. Tickets are for a specific date with no time slot; online tickets can be rescheduled until 18:00 the day before. Dogs are allowed.

visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Clear, calm days, from opening time. In fog or strong wind the views are lost and the walls are unpleasant.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Wear shoes with grip: the walkways are uneven granite steps with drops alongside. Check the forecast; skip it in low cloud. Last entry 17:30.

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 4-4.5 hours door to door on its own (needs a call of 7-8 hours or more); with Pena as well, a call of about 10 hours
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Metro, a 40-minute train and bus 434 up a winding hill road. On site, steep uneven steps and exposed walkways; not suitable for wheelchairs or for anyone uneasy with heights.
combinableWith: Palácio da Pena (next stop on bus 434)
Sintra historic centre (Santa Maria trail or bus 434)
tips: No time slot is needed: buy a date ticket online (12 euros) and enter whenever you arrive.
Bus 434 stops at the castle before Pena; if you plan both, visit the castle first and walk along the road to the Pena entrance afterwards.
Last entry is 17:30 and the castle closes at 18:00, earlier than Pena's park.
Check the forecast: in low cloud the views disappear, and in strong wind the exposed walls are hard going. On such a day choose the National Palace instead.
Wear shoes with grip; the walkways are uneven granite steps with drops alongside.
The ticket office closes from 12:00 to 13:00; the ticket machines keep working.
The marked Santa Maria trail links the castle and the historic centre (about 1.8 km); on a port day use it only with time in hand.
Closed 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January, and may close at short notice when fire risk is very high.

highlights: Walls along the granite ridge, with views to Pena, the town and, on clear days, the Atlantic
Castle Keep, the last stronghold, at one of the highest points of the walls
Arms Square, the walled square where the garrison gathered
Grain silos cut into the rock during the Islamic period
Church of São Pedro de Canaferrim, now the interpretation centre with archaeological finds
Ferdinand II's tomb for the bones found during his restoration
Close view of Pena Palace across the valley
facilities: Small interpretation center with archaeological exhibits
Benches and rest areas along route

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Not wheelchair accessible. Castle features steep stone staircases, narrow battlements, uneven surfaces, and significant elevation changes. Battlements have sheer drops requiring good mobility and balance. Not suitable for visitors with mobility limitations, fear of heights, or in poor physical condition. No elevator or alternative accessible routes available.
accessibility.visualAidServices: Audio guides available with historical descriptions
accessibility.hearingAidServices: Visual information panels; self-guided exploration possible
